scope: Lexical audit of written game C declarations, known-definition direct-call arity, old-style callback tables and shared-header coverage. SDK headers are excluded through LOCAL_SDK_FILES.json. This does not replace target compilation, ROM assembly evidence, callback/lifetime analysis or strict object verification. Assembly-only functions without a C definition are not inferred.

exceptions.name: heapAllocLocal
exceptions.reason: The canonical allocator is void *(HpHdr *, u32, u16). These callers retain legacy allocation labels, signed sizes or ignored fourth arguments. Canonical adoption failed forced matching builds; actorAllocatePartTable, backdropAllocateViewBuffer and wordMapInitialize are recorded matching constraints.
exceptions.next_evidence: Isolate argument promotion, signed size conversion and IDO call setup in the affected caller; preserve the unused argument until both the ROM and strict object comparison pass.

exceptions.name: fontImageGetGlyphIndex
exceptions.reason: The first argument is a supported character code; the second font argument is unused. fontImageReadGlyph omits the second argument through an unprototyped declaration. Both supplying zero and removing the unused formal from the helper and its other callers fail forced ROM builds.
exceptions.next_evidence: Recover a matching single-argument representation or matching initialization of the unused argument; unsupported character ranges remain explicitly undefined.

exceptions.name: heapDebugNoOp
exceptions.reason: This inactive diagnostic hook has a one-argument K&R definition but receives an ignored allocation address after the heap address. Typed two-argument pointer and integer variants both fail the ROM gate. No portable shared prototype is published for this matching-only hook.
exceptions.next_evidence: Isolate heapDebugReportBlock call generation and the rendering callers before replacing the compatibility definition and declarations; do not remove emitted calls merely because the retail hook is inactive.

exceptions.name: searchTreeFind
exceptions.reason: The node return and tree pointer are established. The pointer-shaped object key view matches; canonical integer-address keys change code in these callers. search_tree_lookup.h remains the canonical integer-key interface.
exceptions.next_evidence: Isolate objectPrepareKindSearch and item lookup key argument scheduling, retaining key allocation extents and strict relocation identities.

exceptions.name: terrainCheckHorizontalObstruction
exceptions.reason: The canonical area_services.h result is u16 directional obstruction flags. The orbit caller retains a signed-word result view; changing to u16 fails the ROM gate, including with an explicitly discarded result.
exceptions.next_evidence: Isolate orbitFollowerUpdate call lowering and preserve the original unused-result instruction sequence before adopting the narrow return declaration.

exceptions.name: overlayLoadFromRom
exceptions.reason: The correct void * result is now shared. The runtime caller retains pointer-width ROM offsets and RAM ranges; canonical u32 ROM offsets plus casts fail the ROM gate, including with an explicitly discarded result. The loader and area consumer use overlay_loader.h.
exceptions.next_evidence: Isolate runtimeMainThreadEntry argument lowering. ROM offsets are numeric cartridge addresses, all target addresses are 32 bits, and the returned end-of-BSS address is ignored here.

exceptions.name: progressReadFieldValue
exceptions.reason: The second K&R formal is overwritten before use and omitted by progressGetValue. Moving it to a local and introducing a one-argument prototype fails the ROM gate. Its original register representation remains an explicit matching exception.
exceptions.next_evidence: Recover a one-argument definition that preserves the field-type register allocation and object bytes; do not initialize a dummy argument merely to silence the audit.

exceptions.name: gPlayerInteractionActionHandlers
exceptions.reason: The original action table mixes pointer/integer argument views and one void-returning pickup handler. Dispatch forwards player and controller addresses and exposes an unspecified result for the void handler. Existing Doxygen contracts describe this incompatible callback ABI; no result or adapter is invented.
exceptions.next_evidence: Trace each callback and every dispatch-result consumer against ROM assembly, then establish a common callback contract or matching per-action adapters without inventing a pickup result.
